question: Which statement correctly represents the location of the meristematic tissue in a plant body?

options.text: At the base of the stem
At the tips of the leaves

solution:
The correct answer is __**At some specific regions**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **Meristematic tissue** in plants is found only at **specific regions** of growth. These regions are responsible for the active division of cells.
 
• The main locations of meristematic tissues include the **apical meristems** (found at the tips of roots and shoots), **intercalary meristems** (at the base of leaves or internodes), and **lateral meristems** (responsible for secondary growth, like the vascular cambium and cork cambium).
 
• These tissues are undifferentiated, meaning that the cells are capable of continuous division and can differentiate into specialized tissues as needed by the plant.
 
• Their specific locations ensure that growth occurs in a controlled and organized manner, such as elongation of shoots and roots or increase in girth of stems and trunks.
